title: Week 8
subtitle: The first appointment is usually around now. Bring your questions — this is the visit where you get to ask them.

baby.size: About the size of a raspberry
baby.development: The heart is beating and can sometimes be seen on an early ultrasound. Arms and legs are forming, and the neural tube — which becomes the brain and spinal cord — has already closed.

you.body: Nausea is often at its worst between weeks 6 and 10. Fatigue is real, not laziness. Your blood volume is rising, which can make you feel breathless on stairs.
you.mind: Many people feel a strange mix of excitement and dread in the first trimester, and then feel guilty about the dread. Both are allowed.

coreActions.title: Book your first prenatal visit
coreActions.why: Most OBs want to see you between 6 and 8 weeks. This visit confirms the pregnancy, dates it, and starts the paperwork that everything else depends on.
coreActions.detail: Expect a urine test, blood pressure, blood work (blood type, Rh factor, anemia, immunity to rubella, and STI screening), and often a dating ultrasound. Bring the date of your last period if you know it, a list of any medications, and your insurance card.

options.label: An OB-GYN
options.detail: A doctor, for a pregnancy you expect to manage in a hospital.

options.label: A certified nurse-midwife
options.detail: Often lower-intervention, longer appointments, and available in most states for hospital births.

options.label: A community health center
options.detail: Sliding-scale fees if you are uninsured or underinsured. Search 'FQHC near me'.
options.note: You can often get prenatal care here even with no insurance.

coreActions.skipIf: You already have a confirmed pregnancy and an appointment on the calendar.

coreActions.title: Take a prenatal vitamin with folic acid
coreActions.why: 400 to 800 micrograms of folic acid a day, started before conception and continued through the first trimester, lowers the risk of neural tube defects.
coreActions.detail: Any prenatal vitamin with 400–800 mcg of folic acid works. You do not need the expensive one. If the pills make you sick, a gummy without iron is fine for now — but tell your OB, because you may need iron separately later.

options.label: Any drugstore prenatal
options.detail: Look for 400–800 mcg folic acid on the label. Store brand is fine.

options.label: A gummy prenatal
options.detail: Easier on the stomach, but usually no iron. Good for the nausea weeks.

options.label: A prescription prenatal
options.detail: If your OB prescribes one, it is often covered. Ask before buying.

coreActions.skipIf: Your OB has told you to take a specific prescription instead.

coreActions.title: Find out what your insurance actually covers
coreActions.why: Prenatal care, delivery, and the baby's first year are three separate billing events. Knowing the deductible now avoids a surprise in the delivery room.
coreActions.detail: Call the number on your card and ask three things: what is my deductible, what is my out-of-pocket maximum, and is my hospital in network. Write the answers down. If you are uninsured, you may qualify for Medicaid — in most states pregnancy raises the income limit substantially, and coverage can be backdated.

options.label: Call the number on your card
options.detail: Ask for the prenatal and delivery benefits summary.

options.label: Healthcare.gov
options.detail: Pregnancy is a qualifying life event, so you can enroll outside open enrollment.

options.label: Your state Medicaid office
options.detail: Income limits for pregnant people are much higher than for everyone else.

coreActions.skipIf: You already know your plan's prenatal and delivery coverage in detail.

alsoKnow.title: If the nausea is unmanageable
alsoKnow.body: There are safe prescription treatments for morning sickness, and you do not have to white-knuckle it. If you cannot keep fluids down for a day, call your OB — that is dehydration, not weakness.

alsoKnow.title: Caffeine
alsoKnow.body: Under 200 mg a day is considered fine — roughly one 12 oz coffee. The limit is about total daily amount, not a single cup.

alsoKnow.title: You do not have to tell anyone yet
alsoKnow.body: There is no rule that says you announce at 12 weeks. Tell the people who would support you if something went wrong, and wait on the rest.

redFlags.text: Heavy bleeding, or bleeding with cramps or pain
Sharp one-sided pain, or pain in the tip of your shoulder
Fainting, chest pain, or trouble breathing

appointments.label: First prenatal visit
appointments.note: Blood work, blood pressure, and often a dating ultrasound.
